notes: Resident population is a hand-assembled patchwork, not a single consistent source: central Damascus city itself uses an IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix figure from March 2025 (residents + IDPs + returnees, the most recent figure found, but a displacement survey rather than a census); most surrounding Rif Dimashq nahiyas (Jaramana, Sahnaya, Douma, Kafr Batna, etc.) fall back to Syria's last general census in 2004 — over two decades old and pre-dating the 2011-2024 conflict entirely; a handful of individual nahiyas (Darayya, Al-Tall, Saidnaya) were updated with 2023 or January-2025 local-authority estimates where a more recent figure could be found. Districts partially inside the bounding box are prorated by area fraction. This mixed-vintage assembly is disclosed explicitly rather than presented as one clean dataset. No real employment data exists: jobs are a flat 40% of resident population, redistributed across OSM buildings weighted by floor area only. Commute flows are an unconstrained gravity model with no real O/D anchor.
